finding: Sticky `templateMode` LATCHES ACROSS A TOOL CHANGE and cannot be reset by the value going away. `GeneratedField` is keyed by `field.name` (ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:341-350) and `ToolStepForm` is only remounted per STEP (`<StepForm key={step.id}>`, StepConfigPanel.tsx:88), so changing the Tool inside one step reuses the SAME GeneratedField instance for any property whose name is unchanged. The effect at :106-108 only ever sets the latch to true; nothing clears it when `value` becomes undefined. Given: tool A declares `days` (integer) and the author inserts `{{ inputs.horizon_days }}` (latch=true); they then pick tool B on the same server, which also declares `days` — `patch({tool, arguments:{}})` (ToolStepForm.tsx:329) clears the value but the latch survives, so the integer field renders as a free-text Input with the caption 'Using a reference — resolved when the workflow runs.' over an EMPTY value. Typing 5 then commits the STRING "5" for an integer argument. Violates INV-4 (typed field replaced by free text) and INV-6 (undocumented, silently-defaulted fallback with a FALSE stated reason), plus a real type corruption.

`entryForServerName` is fed `McpServer.servers`, which is `[]` until the LAZY global store's `loadMcpServers()` resolves (mcp/stores/mcpServer/index.ts:44 fires it from `init`, state.ts:6 starts empty) and nothing on this page awaits it or reads its `loading`/`isInitialized` flags. Given: open `/settings/workflows/:id/edit` on a saved tool step — for the whole first render window `servers` is empty, so `entryForServerName` (ToolCatalog.store.ts:243-249) returns `{kind:'unknown-server'}`, the blocking Alert renders 'This step points at a server called "X", which isn't one of the servers available to you' and the Tool field falls back to a free-text Input. Worse: if `loadMcpServers` ever fails (network / perm), `servers` stays `[]` FOREVER and that false accusation is permanent, with no retry affordance (`isRetryableFailure` excludes `unknown-server`, ToolCatalog.store.ts:278-280). Violates INV-3 (a picker degrades to free text for an enumerable entity) and INV-6 (the stated reason is wrong).

`optionKeyForValue` returns `undefined` when a stored enum value matches no declared option, so the `Select` (ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:236-249) renders its 'Choose a value' PLACEHOLDER while `step.arguments[name]` still holds the old value. This is exactly the defect the round-1 fix closed for the Tool picker (the synthetic '… — not offered by this server any more' option, ToolStepForm.tsx:179-195) and it was NOT closed for enum arguments. Given: a saved workflow with `units: "kelvin"` and an upstream schema that tightened the enum to ["c","f"] — the author sees an unset-looking field, believes nothing is configured, and the workflow keeps sending "kelvin". Silent, and the required-check can't catch it because the key is present.

`optionKeysForValues` DROPS any stored array entry that matches no declared option (`.filter(v => v !== undefined)`), and the MultiSelect commits back through `optionValuesForKeys` (ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:250-263). Given: a saved arg `tags: ["a","legacy"]` where the current schema declares only ["a","b"] — the control shows only 'a', and the moment the author toggles ANY option the commit writes `["a", …]` and "legacy" is silently erased from the definition. This is genuine data loss, and it contradicts the module's own stated principle that undeclared data must survive editing (`splitArguments`, toolSchemaForm.ts:445-451, preserves undeclared KEYS but not undeclared VALUES inside a declared key).

The new `d.error = null` on a SUCCESSFUL `runValidate` wipes a concurrent save/install failure. `save()` writes the install failure into the SAME `d.error` slot (:347) and the panel's new error Alert reads it (BuilderValidationPanel.tsx:98). Given: the author edits a step (`updateStep` → `scheduleValidate`, 400 ms debounce, :237) and immediately clicks Save; the POST/PUT fails at ~200 ms (name collision, or `validate_for_install` diverging on `prompt_file:` against the real bundle root) and sets `d.error`; the debounce fires at 400 ms, `/validate-def` succeeds at ~600 ms and clears `d.error` — the persistent failure Alert the round-1 fix added specifically so the save failure stays visible disappears on its own, leaving a green 'No blocking errors.' (BuilderValidationPanel.tsx:137) while the workflow is in fact unsaved.

`runValidate` has NO generation/in-flight guard: two overlapping calls both write `d.validation` (and now both write `d.error = null`) in completion order, not issue order. Both callers are live — `load()` fires one immediately (:192) and every mutation schedules another (:227/237/256/267/275). Given: the mount-time validate is slow (1 s) and a post-edit validate is fast (100 ms), the STALE result lands last and becomes the panel's findings, the StepList's per-step invalid markers (StepList.tsx:39-42) and the Save gate (`hasErrors`, WorkflowBuilderPage.tsx:61) — all describing a definition the author no longer has. The `d.error=null` added this round widens the blast radius to the save-error slot.

`humaniseInstallError` falls back to the RAW api-client message for anything that is not a parseable validator finding, and both consumers render that raw string as prominent copy: an Alert TITLE (BuilderValidationPanel.tsx:115-126) and a toast (WorkflowBuilderPage.tsx:93). `core.ts:715` builds `HTTP error! status: ${status} - ${textResponse}` from the whole response body, so a 502 from a proxy or a 500 with an HTML body puts an entire error page into the Alert title. This is precisely the leak the same round-1 round guarded against for the tool catalog (`describeFetchError`, ToolCatalog.store.ts:68-93, which explicitly cites this exact string) — the mitigation was not applied at the save/validate boundary, so INV-1's 'no machine string reaches the author' still fails on the most common failure of all.

The `inflight` Set and `generation` Map live in the LOCAL store's `actions` closure, i.e. one per ToolStepForm MOUNT, while the cache they protect (`sessionCatalogs`) is module-level and per builder SESSION. `publish` only writes the cache on COMPLETION (:140-145), never on start. Given: step A's form starts `listTools` for server S; the author clicks step B before it resolves — `StepConfigPanel` remounts the form (`key={step.id}`), the fresh catalog store has an empty `inflight`, empty `byServerId` and (still) an empty session cache, so it issues a SECOND `GET /api/mcp/servers/{id}/tools` for the same server. That re-handshakes a stdio MCP server, which is the exact cost the WeakMap was introduced to eliminate (header note :16-24). Marking the entry in the session cache at request start (or hoisting `inflight` into the scope) is what would actually close it.

The `pendingNumberClear` blur-deferral DELETES a previously-committed argument when the author abandons the field on a NaN-intermediate buffer. The kit emits `onChange(undefined)` for both 'cleared' and 'partial' (input-number.tsx:47-50), which sets the flag (:221-223); on blur the kit's own handler takes the `Number.isNaN` branch and RESTORES the display without re-emitting (input-number.tsx:56-67), then calls the consumer `onBlur`, which unconditionally `commit(undefined)` (:228-232) and `commitField` deletes the key (ToolStepForm.tsx:261). Given: `days: 5`, the author selects-all and types `-` (intending -3) then tabs away — the display flashes 5 and the `days` argument is REMOVED from the definition rather than left at 5. Same for `1e` / `1e-` / `.`. The flag needs to distinguish 'buffer empty' from 'buffer unparseable'.

A free 'Additional arguments' row silently VANISHES mid-edit the moment its key matches a declared property. `commitRows` patches `{...known, ...rowObj}` (:255) and sets `lastPushed` to the ROW object (:254); `splitArguments` then classifies that key into `known`, so `extra` no longer contains it, `incoming !== lastPushed.current` and the resync effect (:239-247) rebuilds `rows` WITHOUT it. Given: the author types 'location' (a declared field) into an Additional-arguments key box — at the keystroke that completes the name the whole row disappears from under the cursor and the half-typed value is transplanted into the generated field above. Reachable on every schema whose property names an author might plausibly retype, and it also fires when the author is trying to override a spilled `overflowNames` property that IS declared.

The round-1 addition `.filter(s => s.enabled)` makes a step that points at a DISABLED (but perfectly accessible, registered) MCP server resolve to `unknown-server`, whose copy asserts it 'isn't one of the servers available to you' (ToolCatalog.store.ts:267). Given: an admin temporarily disables server 'weather' and the author opens a tool step that uses it — the builder tells them the server does not exist, drops them into hand-entry, offers no 'Try again' (`isRetryableFailure` excludes it) and offers no hint that the fix is to re-enable the server. INV-6 requires the escape hatch to carry a TRUE stated reason; this one is false. The `unknown-server` variant needs a `disabled-server` sibling.

`optionKeyOf` collides for distinct declared enum values that stringify identically: `1` → "1" and `"1"` → "1"; `null` → "null" and `"null"` → "null". `enumOptions`/`choiceOptions` (:236-250) therefore emit two options with the SAME `value`, and `optionValueForKey` (:389-391) resolves a key by `find(o => o.value === key)` — always the FIRST. Given a tool declaring `{"enum": [1, "1"]}`, choosing the second (string) option commits the NUMBER 1; the picker also has a duplicate React key. Bounded (mixed-type enums are uncommon) but the round-trip is silently lossy and `matchOption`'s lenient second pass (:371) actively depends on this key equality, so it cannot simply be tightened without also fixing the option keys.

INV-3 is violated for any user with more than one page of MCP servers. `McpServer.servers` is a PAGINATED slice (`pageSize: 10`, mcp/stores/mcpServer/state.ts:12) and `entryForServerName` resolves the step's server name only against that slice, so an accessible server on page 2+ resolves to `unknown-server` and the Tool field degrades to free text with a false reason. The code documents this (ToolCatalog.store.ts:227-233) as inherited from the Server picker and defers it, but a documented invariant violation in a reachable state is still a violation — and the Server picker below it will also be missing the same servers, so the author has no way to re-pick correctly either.

The drift guard's emit-site scanner matches only the literal identifier `ValidationError` (:2217) behind a `src.contains("ValidationError")` pre-filter (:2372), so a construction reached through an ALIAS is invisible to it — and invisible SILENTLY, unlike every other hole (which routes into `scan.problems` and fails loudly). Given a future `use crate::modules::workflow::validate::ValidationError as VE;` followed by `VE::err("semantic", "WORKFLOW_NEW_THING", …)`: the file still contains the string 'ValidationError' (from the `use`), so it is scanned, but no code is extracted; the new code is neither in `emitted` (so `unregistered` passes) nor added to `VALIDATION_CODES` (so `stale` passes) nor required to have `HUMAN_COPY` — and it reaches the author as the raw wire message, which is the precise failure INV-1 exists to prevent. Verified the guard is NOT vacuous today: I independently recovered 41 emit sites → 41 codes, `VALIDATION_CODES` has exactly those 41, and `HUMAN_COPY` has exactly those 41 keys. Rejecting a `use … as …` alias in the scanner (a `problems` entry) would close it.

`scan_roots` adds the desktop crate only `if desktop.is_dir()` while asserting `is_dir()` for the server root inside `scan_emitted_codes` (:2350-2355). Given the desktop crate is moved or renamed (`src-app/desktop/tauri/src` → anything else), that root is silently dropped and any `ValidationError` it emits stops being guarded — with no failure. Every other drift-guard hole in this module is deliberately loud; this one is not. Low because the desktop crate emits no findings today (verified: zero `ValidationError::` sites under `src-app/desktop/tauri/src`).

INV-2's 'can take the user to that step' is implemented as `store.selectStep(stepId)` only — there is no scroll/focus move (`grep scrollIntoView` over modules/workflow: none). WorkflowBuilderPage stacks StepList/StepConfigPanel ABOVE BuilderValidationPanel and only goes side-by-side at `md` (:195-204). Given: a 390 px viewport with several steps, the author reads a finding at the bottom of the page and clicks it — the config panel, which is what changed, is entirely off-screen above, so the button appears to do nothing. The invariant is technically satisfied and visibly not.

The `serverId &&` half of the 'Try again' guard is dead. `isRetryableFailure` is true only for `unreachable` / `no-tools` (ToolCatalog.store.ts:278-280), and both are produced exclusively inside `load`, which is only ever called with a non-null `serverId` (:145). So the condition can never be the thing that hides the button, and a reader is led to believe there is a retryable-but-unresolvable state that does not exist.

`WORKFLOW_LEVEL` is exported with a doc comment claiming it is 'part of the returned map's contract', but the only reader in the tree is `indexFindingsByStep` two lines below (:309). No component, store or non-test module imports it — `StepList` looks up step ids only, as the comment itself concedes. CODING_GUIDELINES §15: a `pub`/`export` with no external consumer. Make it module-private, or give it a consumer.

`toolStepNewSurface` (:679) and `toolStepFallbackSurface` (:704) render `<ToolStepForm store={store} step={newToolStepFixture|toolStepFixture} />` — the MODULE-LEVEL fixture object, not the step held in the store they just seeded. Every `patch()` those surfaces make lands in the store while the `step` prop stays frozen, so any interaction in the gallery (pick a server, type a tool name) produces no visible change and the runtime-health / design-critic passes over these two surfaces cannot exercise them. The sibling `toolStepSchemaSurface` (:658) does it correctly by going through `StepConfigPanel`; these two should too.

`humaniseInstallError` fabricates a wire type with `{...} as ValidationError` (:384-389), deliberately omitting `severity`. The `as` cast defeats excess/missing-property checking, so if the generated `ValidationError` ever gains a required field the OpenAPI regen + `tsc` will NOT flag this construction — the one place in the module that builds a wire object by hand rather than receiving it. A typed literal (with `severity` supplied explicitly) would restore the contract check that the rest of the file relies on.

REJECTED — WeakMap leak / dropped live session. `defineLocalStore.use()` stores its proxy in a `useRef` and returns the SAME object for the mount's lifetime (sdk/packages/framework/src/store-kit.ts:631-654), so the scope key is stable for the whole editing session (cache hits work) and becomes unreachable at unmount (entry collectible). Two concurrent builders get two distinct proxies and therefore two distinct Maps — no collision. Nothing module-level holds a strong reference to a scope.

REJECTED — a stale response winning after `invalidate`. Traced both orders: `invalidate` bumps `generation` and clears `inflight`/cache/state (:211-218); the older promise's post-await checks (:183, :191) see the bumped generation and return without publishing, and its `finally` (:202) is generation-guarded so it does not delete the RETRY's `inflight` entry. Double-clicking 'Try again' is also safe (gen 2 wins, gens 0/1 discard). No path leaves an entry permanently `loading` either: the only writer of `loading:true` is `load` itself, which always either publishes or is superseded by an `invalidate` that deletes the entry outright.

REJECTED — the synthetic 'not offered by this server any more' option being re-committed as if real. The Combobox `onChange` returns early when the chosen value equals `step.tool` (:327-330), and the synthetic option's value IS `step.tool`, so pressing it is a no-op; no patch, no save-path difference. Its `storedToolMissing` gate also recomputes to false the instant a real tool is chosen, so it cannot linger in the option list.

REJECTED — the pending InputNumber clear being LOST on unmount (step switch / tool change / Save). Every unmount trigger here is a pointer or keyboard interaction with another control, and focus (hence `blur`) moves on mousedown, before the click handler that causes the unmount runs; the deferred `commit(undefined)` therefore lands first, and `updateStep`'s immer `set` is synchronous, so a subsequent `save()` reads the committed def. The real defect in this machinery is the OPPOSITE direction (an unparseable buffer deleting a good value) — logged separately.

REJECTED — `no-tools` mis-describing an UNREACHABLE server as one that 'answered but publishes no tools'. Checked the backend: `list_server_tools` (src-app/server/src/modules/mcp/handlers/runtime.rs:69-95) propagates `session.list_tools()` errors, so an unreachable/failed handshake is a non-2xx and lands in the `catch`, not in `failureForToolList`. A 200 with an empty array really does mean the server served zero tools, and the 403 → `no-permission` mapping matches the handler's `USER_NO_ACCESS` forbidden exactly.

REJECTED — `parseInstallError` being dead machinery. Verified the producer: `validate_for_install` formats `"[{layer}/{code}] {location}: {message}"` (validate.rs:523-532) and it IS on the builder's save path — `dev::update_user_workflow_definition` calls it before touching the bundle (handlers/dev.rs:562) and it is bound to `PUT /workflows/{id}/definition` (routes.rs:73-76). `AppError::bad_request` surfaces that message through `core.ts`'s `errorResponse.error`, so the regex matches real traffic.

REJECTED — `VALIDATION_CODES` changing from `pub const` to `#[cfg(test)] const` breaking a consumer. Grepped the whole server crate, the desktop crate and the integration tests: no reference outside `validate.rs` itself (the only user is `use super::VALIDATION_CODES` in the guard module). Not part of any serialized/OpenAPI surface either.

REJECTED — the drift guard passing VACUOUSLY today. Reproduced its three inputs independently: 41 `ValidationError::{err,at,warn}` emit sites outside `#[cfg(test)]` yielding 41 distinct codes; `VALIDATION_CODES` contains exactly those 41; `HUMAN_COPY` has exactly those 41 keys (zero in either difference). Its anti-vacuity asserts are all present and reachable: root `is_dir` (:2350), non-empty file list (:2358), non-empty `emitted` (:2598), missing/renamed `const HUMAN_COPY` → `Err` → panic (:2469, :2625), zero parsed keys (:2631), and `problems` failing loudly on any unreadable construction (:2588). The residual hole is the alias case, logged separately.
